youtube.title: Hunyuan3D: free AI turned 3 lamps into 3D (71/100)
youtube.description:
Not sponsored. No affiliate link, and Tencent didn't pay for this.

Hunyuan3D is a free AI from Tencent: you give it a photo, it gives you a 3D model. We gave it 3 desk lamp photos on its free demo page, one try each, no account.

Lamp 1 was shiny metal, and it fell apart into 6 pieces. Lamp 2 worked, but it kept the table too. Lamp 3 came out clean, in one piece. Each took about 20 seconds.

Our score: 71/100 (quality 28/50, speed 15/15, free plan 18/25, price 10/10).
Good for: quick 3D shapes of matte things. Not for: anything shiny or metal.
Tip: shiny surfaces confuse it, so photograph matte objects on a plain background.

Free: about 6 models a day with no account (grey shapes only). Colours need an account. Paid: $9 a month (Hugging Face's paid plan).
All the scores and our 3D ranking: specimindlab.github.io/001 (link in our channel profile)

Lamp photos: Roger Bradshaw, Andrej Lišakov and Aashish Chandra on Unsplash.
Licence note: Hunyuan3D's licence doesn't cover the EU, the UK or South Korea.

youtube.title: TRELLIS 2: a drawing to a 3D dragon in 41 seconds
youtube.description:
Not sponsored. No affiliate link. TRELLIS 2 is a free, open-source AI from Microsoft and nobody paid for this test.

You give it one picture, it gives you a 3D model. We gave it one cartoon dragon drawing on its free demo page, one try, no account. 41 seconds later we had a full 3D dragon, with the wings, the horns and the claws.

The catch: from the side, which the drawing never showed, the tail is flat like a paddle. And without an account you can look at the model but you can't download it.

Our score: 72/100 (quality 35/50, speed 12/15, free plan 15/25, price 10/10). That's our best 3D tool so far, one point above Hunyuan3D.
Good for: turning sketches into 3D drafts. Not for: when you need to download the file for free.
Tip: cut the background out of your drawing before you upload it.

Free: 1 try a day with no account. Paid: $9 a month (Hugging Face's paid plan).
Our 3D ranking and all the scores: specimindlab.github.io/002 (link in our channel profile)

Dragon drawing: void (@voidhve) on Unsplash.

youtube.title: Midjourney: $10 to start, $60 to keep it private
youtube.description:
Not sponsored. No affiliate link, and Midjourney didn't pay for this.

Midjourney makes images from your words. It has no free plan, so we didn't test it and we don't give it a score. Here's what your money gets you, from their own pages.

The cheapest plan is $10 a month. That buys about 800 images, roughly 1.3 cents each.
The catch: on the $10 and $30 plans, everyone can see the images you make. Keeping them private starts at $60 a month.

Good for: mood boards you don't mind sharing. Not for: client work that has to stay private.

The full price breakdown and every source: specimindlab.github.io/003 (link in our channel profile)

The diagram is our own drawing, made from Midjourney's public pages. No Midjourney images are shown.
